:::{#sol-matmul-product-of-sums-practice}

No.
On the left,
$\matr{A} + \matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
so

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{A} + \matr{B})
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 & 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 0 & 0 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 0 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

On the right,
the same rule gives
$\matr{A}\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\matr{A}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
and
$\matr{B}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
so

$$
\matr{A}\matr{A} + 2\matr{A}\matr{B} + \matr{B}\matr{B}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

The entries in position $(1, 2)$ differ, $1 \ne 2$,
so the two [matrices](#def-matrix) are not [equal](#def-matrix-equality).
The rule for numbers fails because
$\matr{B}\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
differs from $\matr{A}\matr{B}$:
@thm-matmul-product-of-sums gives
$\matr{A}\matr{A} + \matr{A}\matr{B} + \matr{B}\matr{A} + \matr{B}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
which does match the left side.

:::
